A_target.statement:
The [[Definition:Natural Logarithm|natural logarithm]]:
:$\ln: \struct {\R_{>0}, \times} \to \struct {\R, +}$
is an order-preserving [[Definition:Group Isomorphism|group isomorphism]].
Hence theorems about sums of real numbers transfer to theorems about products of positive reals.

B_source.statement: Statements about the [[Definition:Additive Group of Real Numbers|additive group of real numbers]] $\struct {\R, +}$ and its ordering.

substitutions.the additive group of reals: the multiplicative group of positive reals

derived.an additive statement: the corresponding multiplicative statement, obtained by exponentiating
derived.the arithmetic mean inequality: the geometric mean inequality, its image under the isomorphism

validity_conditions: The logarithm is a bijection from the positive reals to the reals carrying products to sums, so it is a group isomorphism and every group-theoretic statement transfers.
Order is also preserved, so inequalities transfer as well as identities; this is what turns statements about arithmetic means into statements about geometric means.
Statements involving addition of positive reals do not transfer, since the logarithm does not relate that operation to anything on the additive side.
proof_plan:
By [[Logarithm is Strictly Increasing]], $\ln$ is an order-preserving [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] $\R_{>0} \to \R$, with inverse $\exp$.
By [[Sum of Logarithms]]:
:$\map \ln {x y} = \ln x + \ln y$
Restate the additive theorem in terms of the abstract group operation and order on $\struct {\R, +, \le}$.
Transport along the isomorphism, replacing sums by products and $0$ by $1$ throughout.
